proposed_from.topic: For finite latent-variable causal DAGs with specified observed alphabets, known qualitative functional nodes W, observed support literals Pi, and named x,y, construct FID-S(G,W,Pi,x,y): a terminating graph/support algorithm returning inconsistency, a support-valid formula for P_x(y), or two finite compatible models with identical observed law and unequal target. Prove completeness via a bounded functional-support hedge grammar and support-preserving latent lifting theorem, with explicit certificate/search and rational witness bit-size bounds. Preserve latent-root independence and structural zeros; do not substitute generic real elimination, constrained arithmetic-circuit testing, or the fully observed special case for the latent headline. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A complete fully observed criterion was derived: on every admissible support, identification is equivalent to agreement of deterministic completions sharing observationally reached CPT rows; disagreement yields common-support rational pairs with denominator at most 8nm and target gap at least 3/4, while agreement gives a guarded g-formula. Exact Fraction checks covered 744 realizable supports, 8,928 query/support cases, and 458 constructed NONID pairs; inconsistent clauses, absent treatment support, intervention-exposed rows, cancellation, and the supported bow were tested, with no current-paper collision found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the latent lifting theorem that every residual failure yields a bounded local response obstruction extending to two full independent-latent models with the same observed law/support and different target, and conversely yields a support-valid formula; derive its obstruction grammar and global rational certificate bounds. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaust the binary graph U->A,B; V->A,C; A->B->C with independent U,V over its 4,096 deterministic skeletons and all observed supports of size at most four for P_{A=a}(C=c); any nonextendable proposed certificate, wrong formula, or proved real separating fiber without a rational pair stops or pivots the run. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level results are Shpitser--Pearl hedge completeness and Chen--Darwiche's 2024 and 2026 results. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its separability and parent conditions, while Theorem 18 assumes \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem identifies the declared zero-and-positive support-literal regime introduced here. Chen and Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 establish soundness of formula-returning state-based algorithms under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law, not completeness under those constraints or an exact-support paired-witness trichotomy. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash establish sound-and-complete gID for positive observational laws, but neither arbitrary declared support faces nor exact-support rational paired witnesses are part of that result. The explicit latent bow \(\mathcal B_0\) is resolved state by state even though ordinary ID fails, Theorem 15 elimination leaves the bow, Theorem 18's premise is false because \(\Pr(A=1)=0\), and the 2026 input regime excludes the face because \(A=1\) remains a valid state in \(\Omega_A\) but has zero observational probability. The general kernel changes the load-bearing witness step: every terminal obstruction must extend through discarded districts to two full models with the latent-source architecture of \(G\), supplied observed alphabets, named functional rows, identical exact observed support, and individually encoded rational primitives satisfying a total serialized bit bound. Each model uses exactly the root vertices and parent incidences of \(G\), has its own finite latent alphabets and product root law, and need not share root masses with the other witness. Each constructed pair need only have witness-dependent separation \(\Delta>0\). Conversely, absence of an obstruction must reconstruct a guarded observable formula. None of the named comparators proves either direction on this arbitrary declared-support domain.

proposed_from.literature_map: Shpitser and Pearl provide ordinary ID completeness by recursive district decomposition and parity hedge models; Shpitser's 2023 correction requires failure witnesses to be attached to the actual failed query. Chen and Darwiche's functional elimination preserves identification only under stated eliminability and positivity conditions and does not return support-preserving countermodels. Hwang, Choe, Kwon, and Lee characterize the positivity requirements of a chosen formula without a complete support-aware search. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen show general context-specific do-calculus search is incomplete, while Mokhtarian, Jamshidi, Etesami, and Kiyavash obtain completeness for observed-root control contexts by context splitting and positive extensions. Fraser gives complete possibilistic compatibility through possible worlds. Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe give sourcewise latent-cardinality bounds. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim and Duarte and coauthors expose finite response-type polynomial coordinates and sharp numerical programs, not rational exact-support separating-pair bounds. No closer paper located in the focused functional-dependency, structural-zero, support-compatibility, state-specific, or rational-witness searches subsumes the proposed trichotomy or latent lift.
